newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma urges armed groups to give up their struggle.
newsitem.headline: Burma urges armed groups to give up their struggle.

text.p: Burma's top army official urged remaining armed groups in the country to abandon terrorism and join hands with the government to help build a unified nation, state-run newspapers reported on Sunday.

Lieutenant-General Tin Oo, chief of the army and Secretary Two of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) made the comments in an address to officers at the Ministry of Defence, official media reported.
It was Tin Oo's first speech since a mail bomb exploded at his home last Sunday, killing his eldest daughter.
"It is time for a few brethen groups who still remain underground to think seriously amd make the right decision," Tin Oo's said.

"The Tatmadaw (armed forces) is working together with the national brethen groups who have come in to join hands with it and will build the nation together and will also extend a warm welcome to the brethen who will return from underground after realising the truth," he added.

The "underground" forces referred to the Karen National Union (KNU) rebel organisation, and the outlawed Burma Communist Party. The KNU is the last ethnic guerrilla group that has not signed a ceasefire agreement with SLORC.

"It is a time not to do any destructive act if one loves and cherishes the nation and any person who loves the truth and has a clear political outlook must welcome and take part in the efforts for all-around development of the nation," said Tin Oo.

The KNU was blamed for several recent acts of terrorism including the December 25 bomb attack on a sacred Buddhist shrine in Rangoon which killed five people and wounded 17 others. The KNU denied responsibility for the bombing.

The December attack was seen by some analysts as an attempt on Tin Oo's life. Tin Oo, who has often made speeches urging troops to "annihilate" anyone threatening the stability of the nation, was the last senior official to visit the shrine on Christmas Day before the bombs exploded.
Tin Oo was not injured in the April 6 bomb attack at his house. The government said the bomb was mailed from Japan and blamed it on exiled anti-Burma groups.
Tin Oo said in his speech that political organisations in Burma are colluding with "underground destructionists" and foreign media and to disrupt Burma's political, economic and social development.
Tin Oo and other officials regularly attack the opposition National League for Democracy (NLD) party for colluding with foreign supporters to cause instability.
